messages:
Tara: Quick question  my partner and I just had a baby and I want to add them to benefits. I submitted the life event form but the carrier portal still says dependent not enrolled. Hospital wants insurance info for discharge tomorrow. Any fast path?

Evan (People Ops): Congrats! For newborns we usually have a 30-day window to enroll retroactively. If you filed the life event, can you confirm you attached the birth certificate or hospital birth record and the dependent's DOB?

Tara: I uploaded the hospital birth record and filled the form at 10am. I don't see a confirmation email yet. Discharge scheduled for tomorrow afternoon.

Sam - Benefits: If we have the life event ticket and docs, we can issue a temporary coverage letter on company letterhead that verifies dependent coverage effective on date of birth while the carrier processes enrollment. Send an email to benefits@redwood.com with subject EXACT: "NEWBORN ENROLL - Tara K - URGENT" and attach the birth record. We'll generate a signed PDF and also push the file to the carrier as expedited.

BenefitsBot: ✅ Ticket created: #BEN-4688 - "Newborn enrollment / temporary coverage letter". Target response: same day. Please attach docs.

Tara: Done  just sent email with attachments. Thanks!!

Evan (People Ops): I'll flag the ticket for expedited handling. If the hospital still asks for an insurance card at checkout, the temporary letter should work; if they insist on a member ID card, bring the parent's member ID and the temporary letter. We can also request the carrier to issue a digital ID card while enrollment finalizes.

Sam - Benefits: We replied with the signed letter and the carrier upload is in progress. If you need anything else, DM me and we'll follow up with the billing team at the hospital. :baby::confetti_ball:
